title: What competence and recurrent training does EASA Part-145 require of maintenance staff?
seoTitle: EASA Part-145 and Part-66 staff training
description: EASA Part-145 point 145.A.30(e) competence control, recurrent training for certifying staff in each 2 year period under 145.A.35, and Part-66 licences.
shortAnswer: Under Annex II (Part-145) to Regulation (EU) No 1321/2014, an approved maintenance organization must establish and control the competency of everyone involved in maintenance, airworthiness reviews, safety management and compliance monitoring, including human factors. Certifying staff and support staff, who hold Part-66 aircraft maintenance licences, must receive sufficient recurrent training in each 2 year period and at least 6 months of relevant maintenance experience in any consecutive 2 years. The European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) publishes the rules.
keyTakeaways: Point 145.A.30(e) requires the organization to establish and control competency through a procedure and to a standard agreed with the competent authority, including safety management principles, human factors and human performance.

Point 145.A.35(d) requires all certifying staff and support staff to receive sufficient recurrent training in each 2 year period on relevant technologies, organization procedures and safety management, including human factors.

Point 145.A.35(c) requires at least 6 months of actual relevant maintenance experience in any consecutive 2 year period, and 145.A.35(f) requires a competence assessment before any certification authorization is issued or reissued.
Under Part-66 point 66.A.40, an aircraft maintenance licence becomes invalid 5 years after its last issue or change unless it is submitted to the competent authority for verification.
Personnel records must be kept while a person works for the organization and for at least 3 years after they leave or their authorization is withdrawn (145.A.55).
regulator: European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) and national competent authorities of EASA member states
appliesTo: Maintenance organizations approved under Annex II (Part-145) to Regulation (EU) No 1321/2014
Certifying staff and support staff holding Part-66 aircraft maintenance licences in categories A, B1, B2, B2L, B3, L and C
Accountable managers, nominated persons, compliance monitoring and safety management staff

sections.heading: Which EU rules govern maintenance staff competence?

blocks.text: Maintenance staff competence is governed by Commission Regulation (EU) No 1321/2014 on continuing airworthiness, specifically Annex II (Part-145) for maintenance organizations and Annex III (Part-66) for aircraft maintenance licences. The consolidated text is on [EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02014R1321-20260807), and EASA publishes the rules with acceptable means of compliance (AMC) and guidance material (GM) as the [Easy Access Rules for Continuing Airworthiness](https://www.easa.europa.eu/en/document-library/easy-access-rules/easy-access-rules-continuing-airworthiness).

Part-145 places the training and competence duty on the organization. Part-66 sets the licence each certifying engineer or technician must hold. The two work together: a Part-145 organization may only issue a certification authorization within the categories and type ratings on a valid Part-66 licence (145.A.35(b)).

As at November 2026, the current wording of 145.A.30(e) and 145.A.35(d) was introduced by Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2021/1963, which brought safety management into Part-145. Organizations holding a Part-145 approval had until December 2, 2024 to close findings against the requirements that regulation introduced.

sections.heading: What does 145.A.30(e) require for staff competence?

blocks.text: It requires the organization to define, establish and control the competency of all personnel in maintenance, airworthiness reviews, safety management and compliance monitoring. The text of [point 145.A.30(e)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02014R1321-20260807) reads:

blocks.title: Point 145.A.30(e)
blocks.text: "The organisation shall establish and control the competency of the personnel involved in any maintenance, airworthiness reviews, safety management and compliance monitoring in accordance with a procedure and to a standard agreed with the competent authority. In addition to the necessary expertise related to the job function, the competency of the personnel must include an understanding of the application of safety management principles, including human factors and human performance issues, which is appropriate to their function and responsibilities in the organisation."

Three features matter for training design. First, the scope is wider than certifying staff: it includes compliance monitoring and safety management personnel. Second, the procedure and standard must be agreed with the competent authority, so the approach is set out in the maintenance organization exposition (MOE). Third, human factors and safety management understanding are a mandatory part of competence for every role, scaled to responsibilities.

Point 145.A.30 adds related requirements: a maintenance man-hour plan with sufficient, appropriately qualified staff (145.A.30(d)); non-destructive testing staff qualified to a European or equivalent standard recognized by EASA (145.A.30(f)); and nominated persons able to demonstrate relevant knowledge, background and experience in maintenance and a working knowledge of the Regulation (145.A.30(cc)).

sections.heading: How often must certifying and support staff receive recurrent training?

blocks.text: In each 2 year period. Point 145.A.35(d) states that the organization "shall ensure that all certifying staff and support staff receive sufficient recurrent training in each 2-year period to ensure that they have up-to-date knowledge of relevant technologies, organisation procedures and safety management, including human factor issues." Point 145.A.35(e) requires a recurrent training program with procedures to ensure compliance with 145.A.35 and with Part-66.

items: **Recent experience (145.A.35(c)):** at least 6 months of actual relevant aircraft or component maintenance experience in any consecutive 2 year period, meaning work in a maintenance environment exercising certification privileges or carrying out maintenance on systems within the authorization.
**Assessment before authorization (145.A.35(f)):** competency, qualifications and capability must be assessed under an MOE procedure before a certification authorization is issued or reissued.

**Continued validity (145.A.35(g)):** the authorization stays valid only while points (a), (b), (d) and, where applicable, (c) continue to be met, so a lapse in recurrent training invalidates the authorization.

**Understanding of aircraft and procedures (145.A.35(a)):** certifying staff must have an adequate understanding of the relevant aircraft or components and organization procedures before the authorization is issued or reissued.

**Minimum age and production (145.A.35(k), (l)):** certifying staff and support staff must be at least 21, and certifying staff must produce their authorization to an authorized person within 24 hours.

blocks.text: Category A licence holders may only certify on a specific aircraft type after completing category A task training, including practical and theoretical training for each task, demonstrated by examination or workplace assessment (145.A.35(m)). B2 holders exercising the limited privileges in 66.A.20(a)(3)(ii) also need the relevant category A task training and 6 months of documented practical experience (145.A.35(n)).

sections.heading: How does the Part-66 licence fit in?

blocks.text: The Part-66 aircraft maintenance licence is the individual qualification on which a Part-145 certification authorization is based. Part-145 refers to licence categories A, B1, B2, B2L, B3, L and C: line maintenance requires appropriately rated B1, B2, B2L, B3 or L certifying staff, while base maintenance of complex motor-powered aircraft requires category C certifying staff supported by B1 and B2 staff (145.A.30(g) and (h)).

Under point 66.A.40 of Annex III, the licence "becomes invalid 5 years after its last issue or change" unless the holder submits it to the issuing competent authority to verify that its details match the authority's records. Any certification privilege based on the licence becomes invalid as soon as the licence does. A Part-145 organization may submit the paperwork on the holder's behalf if its exposition includes a procedure for this.

Part-66 itself is being modernized. EASA's September 2025 revision of the Easy Access Rules incorporates Corrigendum II to ED Decision 2023/019/R on the review of Part-66 and new training methods and teaching technologies. EASA notes that Regulation (EU) 2025/111 is not yet incorporated in that revision and will be included in the next one, planned for 2026.

sections.heading: How can a Part-145 organization map staff obligations to evidence?

blocks.text: A competent authority auditor will usually sample a certifying engineer's file and test it against each point of 145.A.35. blocks.text: Because 145.A.35(g) ties authorization validity to continued compliance, many organizations track recurrent training due dates as authorization expiry dates. The general method in [how to build a training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix) and [how to set up verification of competency](/guides/how-to-set-up-verification-of-competency) applies.

sections.heading: What staff records must a Part-145 organization keep?

blocks.text: Records of the qualifications, training and experience of personnel involved in maintenance, compliance monitoring and safety management. Under point 145.A.55(d), records for certifying staff and support staff must also include the details of any Part-66 or equivalent licence, the scope of certification authorizations issued, and particulars of staff who held limited or one-off authorizations.

Personnel records "shall be kept for as long as a person works for the organisation, and shall be retained for at least 3 years after the person has left the organisation, or after an authorisation issued to that person has been withdrawn." Staff must be given access to their records on request and a copy when they leave. Records of management system key processes under 145.A.200 must be kept for at least 5 years (145.A.55(c)). For preparing these files, see [how to prepare training records for an audit](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry defines the competence standard required by 145.A.30(e) for each role, including the human factors and safety management elements, as structured knowledge points with assessment criteria before any training is written. Recurrent training content can then be traced to the changes in technology, procedures and safety management that 145.A.35(d) requires it to cover in each 2 year period.

faqs.q: Is recurrent training required every 2 years or every 24 months?
faqs.a: The rule says "in each 2-year period" and requires the training to be sufficient to keep knowledge up to date. It does not prescribe hours. The organization defines the interval, content and tracking method in its recurrent training program and MOE procedures, within the 2 year requirement.

faqs.q: Does 145.A.30(e) apply only to certifying staff?
faqs.a: No. It covers the competency of personnel involved in any maintenance, airworthiness reviews, safety management and compliance monitoring. Mechanics without certification privileges, planners, quality staff and safety managers all fall within the competence procedure, with human factors and safety management understanding scaled to their role.

faqs.q: What happens if a certifying engineer misses recurrent training?
faqs.a: Under 145.A.35(g), continued validity of the certification authorization depends on continued compliance with points including 145.A.35(d) on recurrent training. If recurrent training lapses, the authorization should be treated as invalid until the requirement is met again and, where needed, the person is reassessed.

faqs.q: Does Part-66 require refresher training to keep the licence valid?
faqs.a: Point 66.A.40 requires the licence to be submitted for verification so it does not become invalid 5 years after its last issue or change. Ongoing training obligations sit mainly with the Part-145 organization, which must provide recurrent training in each 2 year period for the staff it authorizes.
